What evidence links media content to daily stock market behavior, and does that link extend to trading volume and return volatility as well as price?
Media content extracted from financial news correlates with daily stock market behavior, showing up in trading volume and return volatility patterns consistent with an investor psychology channel.
noise trader model arbitrageur belief shock price volume prediction versus information-based account

Under what assumptions does a noise trader model populated with rational arbitrageurs predict that an unfounded belief shock moves prices and trading volume, and how does that prediction differ from a story built on genuine new information?

A noise trader model with risk-averse arbitrageurs implies that an irrational belief shock can move both prices and volume even without any change in fundamentals, a pattern distinct from what a genuine news event or already-priced-in information would produce.
content analysis dictionary coding word sense ambiguity category assignment large text corpus reliability

A quantitative content analysis scheme has to decide, for a word carrying several distinct senses, which semantic category it belongs to -- are those disambiguation choices dependable enough to trust the resulting word counts over a large corpus?

Content analysis built on a fixed word-category dictionary must resolve multi-sense words through explicit disambiguation rules before the resulting category counts can be trusted as a quantitative measure across a large corpus of text.
principal components analysis latent factor category counts loading stability year by year look-ahead bias

Does a single latent factor pulled out of many correlated category counts by principal components analysis stay stable when the loadings are re-estimated separately in each time period, and is that stability enough to justify building the factor year by year without peeking into future data?

Principal components analysis applied separately within each period yields loadings on the dominant latent factor that stay stable enough across periods to justify a year-by-year construction of the composite measure without look-ahead bias.

What regression setup for testing return predictability strips out the autocorrelation and bid-ask bounce that daily prices carry from market microstructure noise, so that a new candidate variable's forecasting power can be judged fairly against lagged returns and volume?

Return predictability regressions on daily data need lagged-return and volume controls to soak up autocorrelation and bid-ask bounce before a new candidate variable's incremental forecasting power can be credited to anything beyond market microstructure noise.

Does Granger causality run from a sentiment index to next-day returns once heteroskedasticity-robust inference is used, and can equation-by-equation ordinary least squares stand in for a full vector autoregression?

Granger causality tests linking a sentiment index to next-day index returns can be implemented with heteroskedasticity-robust ordinary least squares run equation by equation, standing in for full vector autoregressive estimation under standard exogeneity assumptions.

Could feedback trading explain why a price drop today shows up as a gloomier media sentiment reading tomorrow, rather than the sentiment reading being what drove the price in the first place?

Feedback trading offers an account in which a falling index pushes subsequent media sentiment lower, reversing the usual causal story and implying that past returns, not sentiment, are doing the forecasting.
trading volume sentiment magnitude next-day prediction transaction cost proxy liquidity disagreement noise trader

Is it the size of a sentiment swing, rather than its direction, that forecasts next day trading volume, and would that pattern favor a transaction-cost explanation over a liquidity-and-disagreement account of why volume moves?

Trading volume the day after a sentiment reading appears to track the magnitude of that reading rather than its direction, a pattern more consistent with disagreement among liquidity and noise traders than with a simple transaction-cost story.

Does the size premium capture where a sentiment-based return predictor actually bites, concentrating its effect in small stocks that individual investors disproportionately hold, and can that pattern be teased apart from an already-known large-cap predictability result?

A size premium channel would concentrate a sentiment-based predictor's return effect in small capitalization stocks, reflecting the disproportionate ownership share of individual investors there and standing apart from any predictability already documented among large caps.
robustness testing sentiment predictability shifted measurement window information release lag exclusion

Does robustness testing that pushes the measurement window past the hours right after news breaks still find the same sentiment-driven return and volume pattern, ruling out a mere short reaction lag as the true cause?

Robustness testing that excludes the window immediately following a news release rules out a short mechanical reaction lag as the source of a sentiment-based return and volume pattern, leaving the sentiment effect itself as the more credible driver.

Does splitting the sample into an earlier calmer stretch and a later stretch widely seen as overvalued reveal a structural break in how strongly sentiment predicts returns, once the same predictive model is re-estimated separately on each subsample?

A structural break in the sentiment-return relationship would show up as materially different coefficients when the same predictive model is estimated separately on an unusually exuberant subperiod versus an earlier, calmer one.
nonparametric regression sentiment return relationship nonlinearity extreme values kernel weighted smoothing semiparametric

When does nonparametric regression reveal asymmetries in how sentiment relates to returns near extreme values that a linear parametric model would miss, and how does a kernel-weighted smoothing stage capture that?

Nonparametric regression that layers local kernel smoothing on top of a parametric residual fit tends to expose curvature and skew in a sentiment-return relationship at the tails, structure a straight-line model would otherwise miss.

Does trading strategy profitability survive once commissions, bid-ask spreads, price impact and capital gains taxes are all subtracted from a return-predictability signal, and does that survival hold up consistently across different subperiods?

Trading strategy profitability built on a documented return-predictability signal shrinks once commissions, bid-ask spreads, price impact, and taxes are deducted, and whatever edge remains needs to be checked for consistency across subperiods.
factor decomposition composite sentiment measure individual components returns volume psychological construct

Does a factor decomposition of a composite sentiment index show its separate ingredient components moving returns and volume the same way the aggregate does, evidence that would tie the composite to a real psychological construct rather than an arbitrary statistical blend?

A factor decomposition of a composite sentiment measure would show each individual component reproducing the aggregate's relationship with returns and volume, supporting a psychological interpretation of the composite over a purely statistical one.
risk return tradeoff sentiment return relationship conditional volatility proxy required return

Could an ordinary risk return tradeoff account for the sentiment-return relationship, with the sentiment measure simply standing in for shifts in conditional volatility that justify a lower required return, rather than picking up something distinct about investor psychology?

A risk return tradeoff explanation would treat the sentiment-return relationship as a byproduct of conditional volatility changing the compensation investors require, leaving no independent role for sentiment beyond that risk channel.
